title: Stockpiling Uranium to Secure Energy Sources for Shift Towards Nuclear Energy
what_it_is: Stockpiling Uranium to Secure Energy Sources for Shift Towards Nuclear Energy

sections.label: No uranium stockpiling plans
sections.summary: There are no plans for uranium stockpiling, and any deployment decision requires detailed studies of safety, reliability, affordability and environmental sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: As such, we have no plans for uranium stockpiling.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Any deployment decision will require detailed studies of the safety, the reliability, the affordability and also the environmental sustainability of nuclear energy in our local context.

sections.label: SNRSI nuclear scholarships and researchers
sections.summary: SNRSI has awarded 30 postgraduate scholarships and developed around 40 researchers, aiming for about 100 experts in the medium to long run.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Over the last decade, SNRSI has awarded 30 scholarships for postgraduate studies in areas related to nuclear science and engineering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Thus far, SNRSI has also developed a pipeline of around 40 researchers specialising in radiobiology, radiochemistry and nuclear safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We aim to build a pool of about 100 experts in the medium to long run.

sections.label: No nuclear energy decision yet
sections.summary: No decision on nuclear energy has been made, and Singapore must wait for small modular or Generation 4 reactors to be deployed commercially and understand their safety profile.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I think the Member presupposes that we have made a decision on nuclear energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And as I have earlier on, when I addressed the Parliamentary Question, I have said that we have not made a decision.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Member has to appreciate that very conventional nuclear reactors, the older versions, the Generation 1, Generation 2, the safety buffer zone is actually beyond even our radius or any part where you can talk about in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, we have to wait to a small modular reactor, or the newer Generation 4 type of thermal reactors to be deployed commercially and for us to understand the safety profile before we make a decision.

sections.label: Low carbon energy import plans
sections.summary: Conditional approvals cover up to four gigawatts of low carbon energy imports, with geothermal exploration and an ammonia pilot project also underway.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have also gone into Requests for Proposal (RFPs).

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We have given conditional approvals for up to four gigawatts of low carbon energy imports from around the region.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are also exploring potentially geothermal energy sources within our country itself.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are also piloting a new pathfinder project for ammonia – end-to-end – from bunkering to the generation of electricity using ammonia, with a view that ultimately, once technologies for a more economical means of transportation of low carbon or green hydrogen can be established, we will also go and use that as one of the sources for us to generate power as well.
